newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia market rates mixed, banks resort to c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Croatia market rates mixed, banks resort to c.bank.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were mixed on Thursday with some lenders cutting their prices due to modest interbank demand, dealers said.
They said the supply of kuna increased slightly after banks had replenished their resources through a central bank bill repurchase operation and Lombard loans.
They had 68 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans this morning but some were expected to repay them by the end of the day, an official told Reuters.
The fresh money market trade totalled 17.5 million kuna, leaving a shortfall of two million kuna in demand despite 30 million left on the supply side, one dealer said.
Most loans were call money at a steady 10.5 percent.
One foreign bank granted an 11-day loan at a lower 9.40 percent rate. One two-week loan was made at 14 percent, up one percentage point from the established rate.
One-month rates ranged between at 13 and 15 percent.

Overnight trade on Wednesday totalled 57.1 million kuna of which 34 million went to a large bank with a shortfall. The rest was used for maintaining mandatory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
